newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian outback "seething" at euthanasia move.
newsitem.headline: Australian outback "seething" at euthanasia move.

text.p: Australia's fiercely independent Northern Territory was seething with outrage over a looming parliamentary move to quash its world-first voluntary euthanasia law, the Territory's leader said on Wednesday.
As the national parliament's upper house Senate prepared to decide the law's fate, Chief Minister Shane Stone said the outback province's rights were being trampled.
"There is seething outrage in the territory over this attack on the rights of territorians to determine their own affairs," Stone told reporters in the central city of Alice Springs.
The Senate is due to vote in the coming days on a parliamentarian's private bill to quash the nine-month-old law. The bill is expected to be passed, although only narrowly.

Kevin Andrews, a leading member of a Christian morals faction within Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal Party, moved with Howard's backing to have the national parliament use its constitutional powers to overturn the law.
The Andrews Bill has already been passed by the lower house of parliament.

But despite opposition from major political leaders, church, Aboriginal and medical groups, the Northern Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act has overwhelming public support, with polls showing 75 percent of Australians back the right to die.

The law allows dying Australians who meet stringent conditions to commit suicide with a lethal pill or injection. Four people have used it to die since it came into operation last July and at least two others are preparing to do so.
